text:
maya: CI smoke on the a5000 pool is red for PR #4821. Fail is on quant-infer-shard-3 — kernel errors + OOM. Suspect driver/toolkit skew after the image bump.

raj: link? can you paste the job URL and failing shard?

maya: https://ci.redwood/runs/98760/4821 - failing shard: quant-infer-shard-3. Logs show kernel launch timeout, then invalid device function, then OOM. small snippet: ```
[GPU 0] Xid (31) Workqueue timeout detected
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
what(): std::bad_alloc
CUDA Driver Version: 520.61, CUDA Runtime Version: 12.3
Invalid device function
```

oliver: invalid device function + driver mismatch usually means PTX vs driver incompat. Which node image was that job scheduled on?

maya: job attr says image: inference-base:cuda-12.3-driver-525.85-2026-03-16, but when I ssh'ed into the node (a5000-3) it reported host driver 520.61. so host/driver skew is real.

sre-oncall: I can see a partial host-driver rollout moving through the pool. Looks like 3 nodes didn't pick up the new driver. I'll cordon + reimage those nodes.

raj: can we rerun the shard on the known-good stable pool to confirm? @ci-bot rerun job quant-infer-shard-3 --pool=a5000-stable

ci-bot: Command received: rerun job quant-infer-shard-3 --pool=a5000-stable. Job queued (run id 98765).

maya: for quick local checks, run this on the node to confirm driver/runtime: ```docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.3-base nvidia-smi && nvcc --version || true```

oliver: if rerun on stable passes, we can blame host driver skew. if it still fails, we need to bisect PR changes vs base.

raj: i'll kick a short repro job on a5000-3 from my workstation: `bazel test //eng/quant:quant-smoke --test_env=CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and watch logs.

sre-oncall: reimaging started for a5000-1/2/3, cordoned. ETA ~6m. pulling inventory of host drivers and pushing to ops dashboard.

ci-bot: Rerun started: https://ci.redwood/runs/98765 (quant-infer-shard-3 on a5000-stable)

maya: Rerun succeeded on a5000-stable. So this is node/driver skew, not the model change. marking PR as flaky-blocking for now.

oliver: good catch. i'll open a rollout rollback PR to stop the host driver rollout and pin the canary image to driver 525.85. @sre-oncall can you upload the node inventory CSV to the rollout dashboard so we can confirm all nodes are consistent before retrying?

sre-oncall: uploaded inventory to #eng-ml and reverted the cluster rollout. will uncordon nodes after reimage completes.

maya: :thumbsup: i'll re-run full premerge once nodes are back in the stable state and then remove the flaky-blocking tag. thanks everyone.

raj: small follow-up — we should add a quick CI check that fails early if host driver != image driver to avoid wasted runs. filing a tiny issue now.

oliver: yep, a preflight check in the runner would save a lot of noise.

maya: also adding a note to the PR description: "do not proceed with host driver rollout until image-driver parity verified".

ci-bot: Reaction :white_check_mark: recorded for run 98765.
